title: Forty Steps To Lunch
pitch: A visitor enters their lunch options and a few moods, then watches the candidates roll down a forty-station contraption where every station runs a real decision method: budget and distance gates, Condorcet and Kemeny voting, a simulated-annealing ember bed, a Monte Carlo robustness court, a Pareto gate and more. A vending machine drops the verdict, a receipt prints, and a leave-one-out audit names the few stations that actually changed the answer, while a shadow run shows what simply taking the first idea would have chosen. Stations can be added, reordered and tuned, and the long game is a machine in which all forty visibly do something.
whyNow: Timeless: lunch recurs daily, and the punchline is measured by the page instead of asserted. It also fills this week's owed humor slot with a working tool rather than a one-liner.

research.summary: The overengineering joke is an established genre with a clear lineage: dictionaries define the Rube Goldberg sense as complex means for a simple end, and a long-running Java repository satirises enterprise software by piling layers onto FizzBuzz. Lunch deciders are a familiar startup exercise, so the gag alone is thin. The depth comes from methods that are real and checkable: Condorcet cycles, the Condorcet family used in Debian leader votes, simulated annealing (named for metallurgy, introduced 1983) and expected value of perfect information as the ceiling on what extra deliberation can buy. The research shapes the mechanic: every station reports a measured effect, a leave-one-out audit finds the load-bearing stations, and an EVPI-style closing stage delivers the annoyingly correct verdict, measured by the page rather than claimed, of how often the extra deliberation changed anything.

facts.claim: Merriam-Webster defines the adjective Rube Goldberg as accomplishing by complex means what seemingly could be done simply, and the Britannica dictionary gives the same sense: doing something simple in an unnecessarily complicated way.
Pairwise majority voting over three or more options can produce a cycle (A beats B, B beats C, C beats A) even when every voter's own ranking is consistent; this is the Condorcet paradox.
Simulated annealing takes its name from annealing in metallurgy (heating, then controlled cooling) and is credited to Kirkpatrick, Gelatt and Vecchi in 1983.

The expected value of perfect information (EVPI) is the most that removing all uncertainty before deciding could be worth; it is never negative and is an upper bound on the value of any other information gathering.
As of the 2024 and 2025 vote pages, the Debian project uses the Condorcet method for its leader elections, and a LinuxFr report describes Debian's variant as the Schulze method.

FizzBuzz Enterprise Edition, a Java repository presented as satire of enterprise software, is a known example of piling layers onto a trivial task for comic effect, with much of the joke in its tongue-in-cheek issue tracker.
Commenters on a Hacker News thread about a lunch-picker site called building one a rite of passage for startups (reported, unconfirmed; one blended result).

inspirations: Cartoon contraptions such as the self-operating napkin
Office lunch-picking wheels and lunch-picker apps
Marble runs and vending-machine coil drops

design.coreLoop: The visitor sets the scene (options, budget, mood, weather), arranges stations on the conveyor, runs the machine, and watches candidate marbles pass each station while a ticker reports what that station measurably did. The receipt then shows the verdict, idle versus load-bearing stations from a leave-one-out audit, win frequency across thousands of perturbed worlds, and whether the first idea typed would have agreed. Tinkering continues toward two badges, all forty stations active and every active station load-bearing, and a shareable link replays the same machine.
sophisticationHooks: Forty-plus real stations in five families (gates, scorers, voters, stochastic searchers, consensus panels), each a pure function whose effect is measured as eliminations, rank movement or re-weighting, or reported as idle.
Leave-one-out ablation, Monte Carlo robustness and an EVPI-style closing stage produce the annoyingly correct verdict, including how often the naive first pick would have won anyway.
Order matters and is discoverable: a lottery before the filters wastes everything downstream, and a Pareto gate stays idle until a dominated option exists, which turns all-forty-active into a puzzle.

Presentation layer: SVG and canvas conveyor with anvil-drop eliminations, an ember-bed annealer, a vending-machine dispenser and a receipt with a hash-derived serial and barcode; machine, menu and daily seed live in the URL hash.
design.scopeForOneDay: Built in one morning: stage engine plus about 42 stations as small pure functions, an ablation and Monte Carlo worker, a conveyor renderer with a handful of station vignettes reused by family, vending machine and receipt, a drag-and-reorder editor with parameters, 24 hand-written lunch options with attributes, a date-seeded daily scenario, a templated copy module (three line variants per station, filled with real numbers), URL-hash state and an about panel. Cut: real restaurant data or maps, accounts, bespoke art per station, sound beyond optional synthesized clunks.
risks: Forty stations of real logic is the main scope risk; mitigated by building five family templates first, then parameterised variants, with a fallback of shipping thirty stations.
Copy volume across stations is large; templated lines filled with numbers from the actual run keep it from reading as canned.
A long animation can drag; skip and speed controls plus a static step list for reduced motion keep it quick.
Unverified: the 2015-era remark that lunch pickers are a startup rite of passage stays out of page copy, or appears as 'as of 2026-10-11, per a Hacker News comment'.
Close kin exist in enterprise-satire repositories; the differentiators are the measured-effect audit and the all-forty-active puzzle, and page copy has to lead with them.

Stage blurbs that cite method origins stay within verified facts (Condorcet cycles, the annealing name, the EVPI definition, Debian's Condorcet vote); other history is omitted. Lunch scores are the visitor's own ratings, labelled as entertainment, not advice.
